audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/herdr-bin.git...

Analyzing herdr-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines architecture-specific sources that point to prebuilt binary releases hosted on GitHub under the official project's repository (https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr). The URLs are constructed using the declared `pkgver`, which is a static value in the PKGBUILD and not computed via command substitution or external calls. There is no `pkgver()` function, so version computation does not involve dynamic execution.

The `source` arrays use HTTPS URLs to downloadable binaries, which is standard practice for `-bin` packages. The `sha256sums` are provided and not set to 'SKIP', meaning the downloads will be verified during source retrieval. No top-level command substitutions, evals, or suspicious function definitions are present outside the `package()` function, which will not be executed due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. Merely sourcing this PKGBUILD and fetching the sources poses no risk of code execution or data exfiltration.

The package installs a single binary into `/usr/bin/herdr`, which is appropriate for the declared purpose. While the binary itself will need auditing later, that is outside the scope of this narrow gate. Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely download and verify the binaries without executing them.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Safe: no dynamic code or unsafe sourcing
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard binary package for `herdr`, a tool to supervise multiple coding agents. It retrieves prebuilt executables from the project's official GitHub repository, specifically from the release page at `https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases`. The sources are architecture-specific binaries for x86_64 and aarch64, and each comes with a corresponding SHA-256 checksum for integrity verification.

The package uses pinned versioned URLs (v${pkgver}) and includes valid, non-skipped checksums, which ensures reproducibility and protects against tampering. The `package()` function simply installs the downloaded binary into the correct location with appropriate permissions. There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network requests, or suspicious operations such as data exfiltration, dynamic code evaluation, or execution of downloaded scripts.

All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for distributing precompiled binaries. The source and checksums match the declared upstream, and no post-install hooks or additional scripts are present that could introduce risk. Therefore, no malicious behavior is detected.
</details>

data.reasoning: Both models correctly identified the PKGBUILD as safe: uses pinned sources with valid checksums, no dynamic code execution, and standard binary installation. No install hooks or other executable files exist.
coverage_issues: Both models failed to verify the prebuilt binary (herdr-0.8.2-x86_64) which executes at runtime. While binary payloads are out-of-scope for packaging audits, this creates inherent risk.
false_negatives: Neither model flagged the lack of binary verification. Users must manually audit the executable since it handles network/filesystem operations.
learnings: Improve file prioritization: Always detect and review .install scripts if present
Enhance risk awareness: Explicitly warn when unauditable binaries are installed
Reduce over-caution: Both models correctly ignored CI/dev files (none present)

data.reasoning: Both models correctly identified the PKGBUILD as safe: uses pinned GitHub releases with valid checksums, no dangerous functions/operations, and standard binary packaging practices. No install hooks or risky files exist.
coverage_issues: Both models failed to verify absence of .install hooks (though none exist)
No review of binary payload (expected limitation for -bin packages)
learnings: Improve file prioritization: Always check for .install scripts even if absent
Enhance PKGBUILD assessment prompts to explicitly verify hook absence
Clarify audit scope documentation: Emphasize payload binaries are out-of-scope for -bin packages
